# Capability index

<!-- @ref LLP 0061#2-the-capability-index-registry-lite-with-witnesses — witnesses, GAP rows, and the joined surfaces -->

Every author-facing capability Snapback has, whether or not the guide
covers it yet. **GAP** rows are capabilities with no page — explicit, owned,
and dated, never silent. Shipped rows carry a code **witness** proving the
capability exists. The surface map below classifies every entry of the two
machine-enumerable registries (server routes, host-ops); `scripts/check-guide.mjs`
joins it against the code on every run, so a shipped surface cannot fall out
of this file unnoticed.

Guide owner: `ccheever`. File gaps as Linear issues in the Exact project
with the Snapback label and `guide-gap` in the title.

<img src="../brand/snapback-mark.svg" alt="Snapback" width="96" />

# The Snapback Guide

How to build an application **on** Snapback — a complete backend that
scales to zero and back up: schema and functions, server-authoritative
data, live queries, ephemeral realtime, auth, and the client arms — taught
intent-first, with code that ran in CI.

**Audience:** agents (primarily) and humans (secondarily) building on
Snapback. In a checkout, read this corpus directly. Outside a checkout, a
running Snapback server exposes the same build-bound corpus at
`GET /_snapback/guide`, individual paths below that prefix, and the complete
single-request projection at `GET /_snapback/guide/flat.md`. Those responses
carry `x-snapback-guide-content-sha256` and
`x-snapback-server-build-commit`, so a consumer can refuse to combine cached
guide bytes with a different server build. Building Snapback itself is a
different job — that's `AGENTS.md` and the LLP corpus, not this guide.

**Start every task here:** check the
[capability index](./capabilities.md) first — it lists everything Snapback
has, including what this guide doesn't cover yet (explicit GAP rows), so
you never build around a feature because you didn't know it existed.

## The map

### Getting started
- [Your first backend](./getting-started/your-first-backend.md) — schema,
  functions, handlers, seed, codegen, load, query.
- [The authoring loop](./getting-started/the-authoring-loop.md) — edit →
  regenerate → acceptance test → inspect.

### Realtime
- [Live queries](./realtime/live-queries.md) — subscriptions, snapshot +
  replace/delta, durable push, the connection axis.

### Auth
- [Sessions and principals](./auth/sessions-and-principals.md) — the server
  derives who you are; scoped queries; logout barriers.
- [Targets — what each one claims](./auth/targets.md) — local vs hosted
  honesty; how to check the server instead of trusting prose.

### Clients
- [The Contract adapter](./clients/contract-adapter.md) — generated
  bindings, one-surface boot, derived optimistic overlays, offline classes.
- [The React arm](./clients/react.md) — hand-wired client, live queries in
  hooks, honest connection state.

### Testing
- [Acceptance testing](./testing/acceptance.md) — headless-first harness,
  vacuous-pass protection, safe server lifecycle.

### Recipes
- [Presence cursors](./recipes/presence-cursors.md) — ephemeral rooms, TTL,
  publish budgets (the cursors-web demo, distilled).
- [Hidden hands](./recipes/hidden-hands.md) — per-principal secrecy, logout
  blanking, lease-bounded offline retention (card-game, distilled).

### Meta
- [Capability index](./capabilities.md) — everything Snapback has, covered
  or GAP.
- [Conventions](./conventions.md) — page rules, snippet classes, link
  policy, freshness.
- [Retrieval eval protocol](./retrieval-eval.md) — how we verify a cold
  agent actually finds these pages.

## How to trust the code here

Every `js`/`ts`/`contract` snippet marked `source=` is a verbatim excerpt
of a file CI executes end-to-end — `scripts/check-guide.mjs` fails the
build if a snippet drifts from its source. Prose can rot; these can't
silently. Pages carry `targets:` and `maturity:` frontmatter so a claim's
scope is always explicit ([conventions](./conventions.md)).

The deeper design rationale lives in the LLP corpus (`llp/`) — every page's
`authorities:` frontmatter names its sources. The demos (`demos/`) are the
full working applications these pages distill.

# Guide conventions

<!-- @ref LLP 0061#design — the corpus rules this file operationalizes -->

These are the rules every page under `guide/` follows. They are adapted from
the Exact guide's conventions (Exact LLP 0365 §1) as a **compatible core plus
Snapback extensions**, so an agent that has used either guide can navigate
the other. `scripts/check-guide.mjs` enforces the mechanical parts.

## Frontmatter

Every `.md` file under `guide/` opens with YAML frontmatter using the **flat
subset only**: `key: value` scalars and inline arrays (`key: [a, b]`). No
nested maps, no block sequences — the checker parses exactly this subset.

Fields (schema: [`frontmatter.schema.json`](./frontmatter.schema.json)):

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | yes | Human title. |
| `id` | yes | Stable dotted id (`clients.contract-adapter`). Used by nav, links, the capability index, and reserved as the resource id for later projections (MCP, console). Never renamed casually. |
| `order` | yes | Deterministic ordering within the section. |
| `audience` | yes | `agent-first`. |
| `capabilities` | yes | Capability-index ids this page claims coverage of (`[]` for meta pages). |
| `authorities` | yes | Repo paths (LLPs and code) this page derives from. Freshness compares these against `reviewed-commit`. |
| `examples` | yes | Demo directories/files that exercise what the page teaches (`[]` if none). |
| `status` | yes | `draft` \| `current` \| `deprecated` — authored lifecycle. |
| `targets` | yes | `[local]`, `[local, cloudflare]`, or `[all]` for genuinely target-independent material. Local-only pages render a banner line (see below). |
| `maturity` | yes | `shipped` \| `partial` \| `design-only`, consistent with the capability index. |
| `reviewed` | yes | Date of the last intentional review — display metadata only. |
| `reviewed-commit` | yes | The commit the page was last reviewed at — the freshness **identity**. Bumping it is a deliberate act in a review pass; no tool regenerates it. `HEAD` is permitted only in the same change that creates or fully revises the page. |

`targets:` and `maturity:` are the honesty boundary made mechanical
(LLP 0060's posture): a page must never generalize a local-target guarantee
into a hosted claim. A `maturity: partial` page names what works and what
doesn't. `design-only` material may appear only inside an explicitly marked
**Design reference** section, never as a technique. Auth pages teach only
behavior witnessed by an acceptance test or the server's own
capability/inspect reporting.

### Banner

Pages with `targets: [local]` start the body with:

> **Local target only.** This page describes the local dev/test target.
> Hosted targets make deliberately weaker or different claims — see
> [auth/targets](./auth/targets.md).

## Headings

Intent-first: name sections for what the reader wants to do ("Subscribe to a
query", "Scope a query to the signed-in user"), not for internal subsystem
names, so grep-by-goal works. Where a page covers an enumerable surface, it
lists **all** of it — sampling is how capabilities go undiscovered. Each
teaching page ends with an **Anti-patterns** section naming what not to
hand-roll.

## Links

Two classes, checked:

- **Corpus-internal links** are relative paths within `guide/`
  (`../realtime/live-queries.md`). They must resolve.
- **Out-of-corpus references** — `authorities:`, `examples:`, and inline
  bridges into `llp/`, `demos/`, `src/`, etc. — use repo-root paths in
  frontmatter and the `repo:` scheme inline
  (`[LLP 0008](repo:llp/0008-local-first-sync-and-realtime.rfc.md)`). They
  must exist in the repo.
- **Cross-repo references** (the Exact guide seam) name the repository in
  prose and may use `repo(exact):` inline
  (`[the Exact guide](repo(exact):guide/index.md)`). They resolve only
  when the sibling checkout exists; the checker warns rather than fails when
  it is absent. The seam is one-directional from Snapback for now
  (LLP 0061 §Relationship).

## Code snippets

Every fenced `js` / `mjs` / `ts` / `tsx` / `json` / `contract` block carries
a declared class in its info string; the checker fails on unclassified
fences in those languages.

- **Transcluded-verified (the default):**
  <code>```js source=demos/todo/tests/acceptance/headless.mjs</code>
  The fence body must be an exact contiguous excerpt of the named file
  (leading indentation may be uniformly stripped; trailing whitespace is
  normalized). The named file must be exercised by CI — a demo acceptance
  suite, package test, or proof script. Drift in the source breaks the
  check, which is the point: the snippet's "this ran" property is inherited
  from CI, and behavioral drift becomes structural breakage. Update the page
  in the same change that changes the source.
- **Fragment:** <code>```js fragment reason="mid-file excerpt"</code>
  Not verified; the reason is mandatory so partial code is a tracked class,
  not an escape hatch.
- **Standalone-runnable:** reserved (LLP 0061 §Design 3). The scratch-app
  assembler is built only when a technique no CI-exercised file demonstrates
  needs a snippet; until then the checker rejects the class with a pointer
  to this paragraph. Prefer adding the technique to a demo or fixture and
  transcluding it.

`sh` fences are illustrative commands and exempt from mechanical
verification; keep them real and current. `text`, `yaml`, and diagram fences
are exempt.

**Exact-dependent snippets** (Contract-arm sources): the text match runs
everywhere with no Exact dependency. The *execution* guarantee is inherited
from the suite that runs the source file — Contract-arm suites are gated by
`SNAPBACK_VERIFY_EXACT`, which merge/release CI pins to `1`, so those
sources are always executed before landing even when a local core-only run
skipped them. The manifest records each snippet's source so a consumer can
see which suite carries its guarantee.

## The capability index

[`capabilities.md`](./capabilities.md) is authored, not generated. Shipped
rows carry a **witness** — a route in the declared registry, a host-op id, a
package export, a generated-manifest field, or a CLI command proving the
capability exists in code. Uncovered capabilities are explicit **GAP** rows
naming an owner and a review date. The checker joins the index's surface map
against the repo's declared enumerations (route registry, host-ops) — every
enumerated entry maps to a capability id or a `notAuthorFacing`
classification.

## The manifest

[`guide-manifest.generated.json`](./guide-manifest.generated.json) is
generated by `scripts/generate-guide-manifest.mjs` — nav tree, per-page
frontmatter, content hashes, capability join, per-snippet status, and the
build identity the corpus was verified against. Never hand-edit it; every
later projection (MCP, admin console, CLI) consumes the manifest rather than
re-parsing the tree.

The same command emits [`guide-flat.generated.md`](./guide-flat.generated.md):
the capability index first, then every page exactly once in manifest nav
order. Its SHA-256 is the manifest's `contentHash`. The guide checker rejects
either generated file when stale. At server compile time, `build.rs` restamps
the embedded manifest's `buildIdentity.commit` to the exact binary build; the
checked source manifest remains the corpus-generation record.

## Freshness

Warning-only, but sound: the checker reports pages whose `authorities:`
changed between `reviewed-commit` and `HEAD` (via `git diff`). Dates are
never identity. Expired GAP review dates and check failures gate; drift
warnings don't (LLP 0061 §Design 3).

# Retrieval eval protocol

<!-- @ref LLP 0061#5-keeping-it-current-ownership-the-diary-loop-and-a-small-eval — the pinned protocol -->

The repeatable check that the guide's discovery wiring actually works: a
cold agent with a real intent finds the paved road through the guide instead
of building around it. This is the Phase 1 exit criterion and reruns after
any discovery-wiring change (the AGENTS.md pointer, the README row, the
index page, the capability index's shape).

## Fixture

A fresh agent context — same family/tier as the repo's primary authoring
agents — cold-started in a Snapback checkout at HEAD with `AGENTS.md` as the
only steer. No prior conversation, no memory of this repo's guide.

## Seed intents

At least three, across feature areas (extend, don't replace, when new areas
land):

1. **Realtime:** "Add a live-updating list of items to an app built on
   Snapback." Expected pages: `realtime/live-queries.md` (and
   `getting-started/` if starting fresh).
2. **Ephemeral:** "Let two users of my Snapback app see each other's
   cursors." Expected pages: `recipes/presence-cursors.md` or
   `realtime/ephemeral-state.md` (GAP-aware: until the ephemeral page
   exists, the recipe is the target).
3. **Auth:** "Scope a query so each signed-in user only sees their own
   rows." Expected pages: `auth/sessions-and-principals.md`,
   `recipes/hidden-hands.md`.

## Budget

The relevant guide page must be loaded within the first ~15 tool uses.

## Rubric

The run passes when the agent:

- (a) loads the relevant guide page(s) within budget;
- (b) plans or implements with the paved technique the page teaches; and
- (c) does **not** reach for the named anti-patterns — hand-wired HTTP glue
  for app data, polling a subscribable query, client-asserted identity.

## Evidence

The transcript of each run is retained under `guide/eval-runs/` (dated
subdirectory per run, one file per intent), referenced from the run's
summary note. A failed intent files a guide gap (see
[conventions](./conventions.md)) and blocks the change that triggered the
rerun until dispositioned.

## Owner and cadence

The guide's named owner (see `capabilities.md` header). Run at Phase 1 exit
and after any discovery-wiring change. Two consecutive runs with a failed
intent escalate to the Exact LLP 0365 retrieval-eval machinery per
LLP 0061's adoption triggers.

## Baseline

The failure exemplars this eval must not reproduce: diary 0010's
connection-state source-reading detour and ENG-22218's hand-wired HTTP glue.

# Sessions and principals

> **Local target only.** This page describes the local dev/test target.
> Hosted targets make deliberately weaker or different claims — see
> [auth/targets](./targets.md).

The one idea (LLP 0039): **the server derives who you are; the client never
asserts it.** In sessions mode, `ctx.auth` comes only from a server-minted
session resolved at one invocation gate covering every entry path — HTTP,
WebSocket, everything. Everything this page teaches is witnessed by
`demos/card-game/tests/acceptance/authority-scope.mjs`, which runs in the
local proof.

Auth mode is per-app schema config
(`auth: { mode: 'dev' | 'sessions' }` in `defineSchema` — see
[your first backend](../getting-started/your-first-backend.md)). `dev` mode
is the trusted-local convenience where tests pass `userId:` directly;
`sessions` is the real thing below.

## Sign in: email code → session credential

The client requests a code and exchanges it. In tests, the code is read
from the server's admin-gated mailbox (a real mail sender fills that role
outside tests):

```js source=demos/card-game/tests/acceptance/authority-scope.mjs
  const requested = await client.authRequestCode(email);
```

```js source=demos/card-game/tests/acceptance/authority-scope.mjs
  const credential = await client.authExchange({
    challengeId: requested.challengeId,
    code: mailbox.code,
  });
```

From then on the client carries the session credential; `AuthCoordinator`
(from `@snapback/contract`) owns custody, refresh, and the logout barrier
for surface-based clients.

## Queries are scoped by the server, not by arguments

A protected query takes **no owner argument** — the definition's
`authScopeField` binds rows to the server-derived principal, and two
signed-in users see disjoint results over the same query:

```js source=demos/card-game/tests/acceptance/authority-scope.mjs
  const [adaResult, graceResult] = await Promise.all([
    ada.client.query('myHand', { args: { gameId } }),
    grace.client.query('myHand', { args: { gameId } }),
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(adaResult.rows.map(({ card }) => card), ['ace-spades', 'queen-hearts']);
  assert.deepEqual(graceResult.rows.map(({ card }) => card), ['king-clubs', 'ten-diamonds']);
```

Trying to smuggle identity through the request body is rejected with a
stable code — assert on it, don't work around it:
`SNAPBACK_AUTH_BODY_AUTH_UNSUPPORTED`.

## Logout is a barrier, not a suggestion

Logging out blanks that principal's live boundaries immediately; other
principals' subscriptions are untouched:

```js source=demos/card-game/tests/acceptance/authority-scope.mjs
  await ada.client.authLogout();
  assert.deepEqual(adaSurface.boundary.current('hand'), []);
```

Offline retention of authorized data is honest too — retained rows survive
a cold boot only until the signed lease's exact deadline; see the
[hidden hands recipe](../recipes/hidden-hands.md) for the full witnessed
sequence.

## Ask the server what auth is actually on

Don't guess from docs — the capability manifest's runtime facts carry
`authProgramReadiness` (a per-facet boolean projection: provider core,
shared invocation gate, connection binding, authorization invalidation,
authorized leases, session activation readiness, ...) plus the active
`AuthMode`. `GET /inspect` (public projection) and the admin inspect carry
it; teach your tooling to read it. This is the boundary rule this guide
itself follows: an auth behavior is teachable only when it has an
acceptance witness or shows as ready here.

**Not shipped yet (explicit gaps):** agent principals and scoped grants
(LLP 0055) and scoped roles/memberships (LLP 0056) are Review-stage
designs — the `/auth/agents/*` and grant routes exist behind the program
fence and are GAP rows in the [capability index](../capabilities.md), not
teachable surface.

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not assert identity from the client** — no `userId` in bodies, no
  owner arguments on protected queries. The server derives it or the
  request is rejected.
- **Do not build auth UI against unwitnessed surface.** Check
  `authProgramReadiness` / the capability index instead of assuming a
  route's existence means its behavior is on.
- **Do not treat retained offline data as unconditionally readable** — the
  lease deadline is exact and enforced client-side too.

# Targets — what each one claims

Snapback is deliberately honest about which guarantees belong to which
execution target. Guide pages carry `targets:` frontmatter for exactly this
reason; this page is the map those banners point to.

## Local (Ibex + SQLite) — the canonical dev/test target

The full local server (LLP 0002) is where every guide technique on a
`targets: [local]` page holds: server-authoritative mutations with one
commit version and read-set validation, live queries over the durable lane,
ephemeral realtime, and local sessions-mode auth with server-derived
principals, connection-bound live grants, auth-invalidation barriers, and
signed authorized-lease offline retention.

**What the local target deliberately does NOT claim** (LLP 0060; the
README's must-not-claim posture): these are local-target guarantees, not
hosted-auth readiness. The local target reports no target-owned external
TLS, no trusted effective-source derivation, no shared authentication
throttle, no multi-replica invalidation, and no sender-constrained browser
credential. Hosted auth is honestly **disabled** on the local bearer
target rather than half-claimed.

## Cloudflare — the hosted proof, as far as it is real

The Cloudflare target (LLP 0014/0040/0049) is a working proof — the All
Aboard demo runs live on it with Durable Objects storage, deploy-time
secrets, gated action egress, and settled idle-to-zero evidence. It is a
narrow proof, not a paved product target: treat any technique on a page
without `cloudflare` in its `targets:` as unverified there, and treat
hosted auth as absent until LLP 0060's contract is implemented and
witnessed.

## How to check instead of trusting prose

A running server states its own capabilities: `GET /inspect` carries the
capability manifest with runtime facts including `authProgramReadiness`
and the active auth mode. When a page's claim and a server's report
disagree, the server is right and the page has drifted — file a guide gap
(see [conventions](../conventions.md)).

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not generalize a local guarantee into a hosted claim.** The gap is
  the product's honesty boundary, and this guide inherits it mechanically.
- **Do not ship a browser bearer credential to real users on the local
  target and call it auth.** That configuration exists for local
  development; LLP 0060 documents why it must not be marketed as more.

# The Contract adapter

> **Local target only.** This page describes the local dev/test target.
> Hosted targets make deliberately weaker or different claims — see
> [auth/targets](../auth/targets.md).

`@snapback/contract` (`packages/snapback-contract`) binds a Snapback
backend into a Contract/Exact app: codegen emits per-function Contract
binding modules, and `createSnapbackContractSurface` wires them to a live
client at boot. You write no data-plumbing — the `.contract` file names
what it uses, and everything between it and the server is generated or
product code. (Contract *authoring* itself — language, components, styling
— is the Exact guide's territory; this page covers the Snapback side of
the seam.)

## Bind functions in the .contract file

Codegen wrote one module per query/mutation under
`snapback/generated/contract/`. The app `use`s them and declares
`query`/`mutation` bindings:

```contract source=demos/todo-v2/surfaces/contract/todo.contract
use listTodos from "../../snapback/generated/contract/listTodos.query.ts"
use createTodo from "../../snapback/generated/contract/createTodo.mutation.ts"
use setCompleted from "../../snapback/generated/contract/setCompleted.mutation.ts"
```

```contract source=demos/todo-v2/surfaces/contract/todo.contract
  query todos = listTodos({})
  mutation addTodo = createTodo
  mutation markDone = setCompleted
```

Actions call mutations with typed args:

```contract source=demos/todo-v2/surfaces/contract/todo.contract
  action toggleTodo(id, completed) mutates markDone
    markDone({ id: id, completed: completed })
```

## What a generated binding is

Small and inspectable — a typed delegate into a runtime-links registry:

```ts source=demos/todo-v2/snapback/generated/contract/setCompleted.mutation.ts
export const descriptor = 'setCompleted';
export type SetCompletedArgs = { id: string; completed: boolean };

export function setCompleted(args: SetCompletedArgs) {
  return getSnapbackContractLinks().setCompleted(args);
}
```

```ts source=demos/todo-v2/snapback/generated/contract/runtime-links.ts
let links: SnapbackContractLinks | null = null;

export function configureSnapbackContractLinks(next: SnapbackContractLinks): void {
  links = next;
}
```

The generated `SnapbackContractLinks` interface enumerates every bound
query, mutation, and ephemeral channel — using one before the bridge is
configured throws, so a missed boot step fails loudly, not emptily.

## Boot: one surface, one idempotent ensure

```ts source=demos/todo-v2/surfaces/contract/main.ts
  const surface = await createSnapbackContractSurface({
    queryName: 'listTodos',
    boundaryKey: 'todos',
    // No hand-written reducers: todo-v2's mutations are IR-tier, so the
    // adapter derives their optimistic overlays from the manifest-embedded
    // plans (Exact LLP 0329 E-B). Apps may still pass optimisticReducers to
    // override per mutation.
    runtime: await import('@exact/contract/runtime'),
    client,
    clientStore,
    userId: ADA,
    manifest: contractDataManifest,
    artifactIndex,
    schemaManifest,
    functionManifest: functionsManifest,
  });
  activeSurface = surface;
```

Then hand the surface's links to the generated registry —
`configureSnapbackContractLinks(surface.links)` — and mount. Before the
surface, boot runs `client.health()` and the **idempotent**
`client.ensureApp({ schema, functions, seed })` (provisions only what's
missing, seeds only empty tables — a reload never resets data; LLP 0034
§5). If the backend is unreachable, the surface may still boot from an
authorized retained snapshot; a true first run fails with the original
network error instead of inventing an empty app.

What the surface does for you:

- **Validates artifacts** — the Contract data manifest is checked against
  the artifact index; stale generates fail with
  `SNAPBACK_STALE_CONTRACT_DATA_*` codes rather than mis-binding.
- **Optimistic overlays** — declarative (IR-tier) mutations get their
  optimistic overlay **derived from the manifest-embedded plan**; a
  rejected mutation republishes authoritative rows and surfaces
  `SNAPBACK_CONTRACT_MUTATION_FAILED`. Pass `optimisticReducers` only to
  override.
- **Live push** — `livePush: true` by default; multi-query apps pass
  `liveQueries: [...]` (each entry a name or `{ name, args }`) bound over
  one shared stream. `onConnectionChange` carries the
  [connection axis](../realtime/live-queries.md).
- **Offline/Parity** — with a `clientStore`
  (`createLocalStorageSnapbackClientStore` /
  `createMemorySnapbackClientStore`) the surface persists retained queries
  and an outbox; it reports capability class `Parity` only when the store
  is configured, the manifest claims `offlineReplay`, and every declared
  mutation has a derivable plan — else `Online`. Honest classes, no
  pretending.
- **Ephemeral channels** — bound as generated links (subscribe + publish
  pairs); see the [presence recipe](../recipes/presence-cursors.md).

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not hand-wire `client.mutate` inside a Contract app.** The generated
  bindings + surface links are the product path; hand-wiring bypasses
  optimistic overlays, receipts, and reconciliation.
- **Do not write optimistic reducers for declarative mutations.** They are
  derived; hand-written ones drift.
- **Do not skip `artifactIndex`/manifest validation by passing stale
  generates.** Regenerate; the stale-rejection codes exist to stop exactly
  this.

# The React arm

> **Local target only.** This page describes the local dev/test target.
> Hosted targets make deliberately weaker or different claims — see
> [auth/targets](../auth/targets.md).

React apps consume Snapback through the framework-neutral client
(`demos/_kit/client.mjs`) **wired by hand** — there is no generated React
binding layer today. That is the deliberate difference between the arms:
the [Contract adapter](./contract-adapter.md) generates the wiring; React
writes ~20 explicit lines per surface. The wiring is small enough to audit,
and this page is the paved version of it — the exact material diary 0010
had to read source to reconstruct.

Boot is identical to the Contract arm: `client.health()`, then the
idempotent `client.ensureApp({ schema, functions, seed })` — never a
destructive reset on reload.

## Wire live queries into state

Bind each live query once, pushing rows and connection state into React
state; keep the handles for disposal:

```ts source=demos/all-aboard/surfaces/react/src/main.tsx
      const liveQuery = client.liveQuery.bind(client) as unknown as LiveQueryFn;
      const delaysLive = await liveQuery('liveTrainStatus', {
        connectionId: CONNECTION,
        transport: 'stream',
        onUpdate: (rows) => setDelayRows(rows as never),
        onConnectionChange: (value) => setConnection('liveTrainStatus', value as never),
      });
      const feedLive = await liveQuery('feedState', {
        connectionId: CONNECTION,
        transport: 'stream',
        onUpdate: (rows) => setFeedRows(rows as never),
        onConnectionChange: (value) => setConnection('feedState', value as never),
      });
      liveHandles = [delaysLive, feedLive];
      setDelayRows(delaysLive.rows as never);
      setFeedRows(feedLive.rows as never);
```

Notes that keep this correct:

- **One `connectionId` per surface.** All of a page's live handles share
  one durable socket; per-handle connection axes still arrive per query.
- **Apply `handle.rows` immediately after subscribing** — the snapshot is
  already on the handle; don't wait for the first push.
- **Dispose on unmount/HMR.** Every handle's `dispose()` runs in the
  effect cleanup (and StrictMode double-mount means a subscribe can resolve
  *after* its cleanup ran — check a `disposed` flag and dispose the
  latecomer instead of leaking it, as `useCursorRoom.ts` does).
- Mutations are direct calls handed down as callbacks:
  `client.mutate(ref, { args, userId })` / `client.action(...)` — the same
  structured results the headless client gets.

## Render connection state honestly

Consume the derived connection axis
(`connecting | live | stale | disconnected` — see
[live queries](../realtime/live-queries.md)) and render degraded states as
degraded: retained rows shown under a `stale` marker, TTL-pruning frozen
while degraded so departed entries stay renderable, resubscribe on
recovery. `demos/cursors-web/surfaces/react/src/useCursorRoom.ts` is the
reference hook for the full pattern (state mapping, `needs_resync`
handling, frozen maps).

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not build a polling loop where a subscription exists** — wire
  `liveQuery` with `onUpdate` into state.
- **Do not treat `stale` as `live`.** The axis exists so the UI can tell
  the truth; collapsing it to a boolean re-creates the all-aboard red-team
  finding.
- **Do not leak handles across HMR/StrictMode remounts.** Track and
  dispose, including late-resolving subscribes.

# Your first backend

> **Local target only.** This page describes the local dev/test target.
> Hosted targets make deliberately weaker or different claims — see
> [auth/targets](../auth/targets.md).

A Snapback backend is a directory — conventionally `<app>/snapback/` —
holding a handful of source-authored `.mjs` files plus a committed
`generated/` tree that codegen produces from them:

```text
myapp/
  snapback/
    schema.mjs        # source-authored schema (the source of truth)
    functions.mjs     # query/mutation/action definitions
    handlers.mjs      # bundled ctx.db handler module (only if you use JS handlers)
    seed.json         # deterministic declarative seed
    generated/        # codegen output — committed, deterministic, never hand-edited
```

You write the first four. Everything under `generated/` comes from
`node packages/snapback-codegen/index.mjs myapp/snapback` and is committed.

## Declare the schema

All authoring helpers come from `packages/snapback-codegen/define.mjs`
(demos import it via the `demos/_kit/define.mjs` shim). A schema is tables
of validated fields, with chainable `.index(...)` and `.sync()`:

```js source=demos/todo/snapback/schema.mjs
import { defineSchema, defineTable, v } from '../../_kit/define.mjs';

export default defineSchema({
  todos: defineTable({
    title: v.string(),
    completed: v.boolean(),
    userId: v.string(),
  })
    // by_user backs the user-scoped live query's index-first lookup.
    .index('by_user', ['userId'])
    // Declared syncable so it can back the restricted syncable-live subset.
    .sync(),
});
```

The complete validator set: `v.string()`, `v.boolean()`, `v.integer()`,
`v.real()` / `v.number()`, `v.json()`, `v.object({...})`, and
`v.optional(inner)`. `defineSchema` also takes an options object:
`ephemeral:` (a `defineEphemeral(...)` — see the
[presence recipe](../recipes/presence-cursors.md); a dedicated
`realtime/ephemeral-state.md` page is a tracked gap), `auth:`
(`{ mode: 'dev' | 'sessions' }` — see
[auth/sessions-and-principals](../auth/sessions-and-principals.md)), and
`requiredCapabilities:`.

The system fields `_id`, `_version`, `_createdAt`, `_updatedAt` are
server-owned. Declaring one is a hard error
(`SNAPBACK_SCHEMA_SYSTEM_FIELD`), and handlers never set timestamps.

## Define functions

There are two authoring styles, freely mixed in one `functions.mjs`:

1. **Declarative plans** (`defineQuery`, `defineLiveQuery`,
   `defineMutation`) — built from expression helpers, deterministic, no JS
   runtime involved.
2. **JS handlers** (`defineJsQuery`, `defineJsLiveQuery`,
   `defineJsMutation`, `defineAction`) — logic lives in a bundled
   `handlers.mjs` and runs against the injected `ctx`.

A declarative query — filter, order, index, and the server-derived user id:

```js source=demos/todo/snapback/functions.mjs
export const listTodosOnce = defineQuery({
  table: 'todos',
  args: {},
  filter: [eq('userId', authUserId())],
  order: [asc('_createdAt')],
  index: 'by_user',
});
```

A JS mutation — the definition names its handler and declares its writes:

```js source=demos/todo/snapback/functions.mjs
export const createTodo = defineJsMutation({
  args: { title: v.string() },
  source: 'handlers.mjs',
  exportName: 'createTodo',
  writes: ['todos'],
});
```

A declarative mutation, for comparison:

```js source=demos/todo/snapback/functions.mjs
export const editTitle = defineMutation({
  args: { id: v.string(), title: v.string() },
  plan: patch('todos', arg('id'), { title: arg('title') }),
  returns: returnChangedCount(),
});
```

`demos/todo-v2/snapback/functions.mjs` is the fully declarative variant of
the same app — the side-by-side worth reading when choosing a style.

## Write handlers (JS style only)

Handlers register on a global and receive only the injected `ctx` — no
imports, no `process`/env, no timers, no network, no direct storage:

```js source=demos/todo/snapback/handlers.mjs
globalThis.__snapbackHandlers = {
  async listTodos(ctx) {
    return await ctx.db
      .query('todos')
      .withIndex('by_user')
      .eq('userId', ctx.auth.userId)
      .order('_createdAt', 'asc')
      .collect();
  },

  async createTodo(ctx, args) {
    const title = String(args.title ?? '').trim();
    if (!title) throw new Error('todo title is required');
    return await ctx.db.insert('todos', {
      title,
      completed: false,
      userId: ctx.auth.userId,
    });
  },
```

The `ctx` surface: `ctx.db.query(table).withIndex(name).eq(field, value)`
`.in(field, [...])`.`order(field, dir)`.`collect()`, plus
`ctx.db.get(table, id)`, `ctx.db.insert(table, values)`,
`ctx.db.patch(table, id, values)`, `ctx.db.delete(table, id)`, and
`ctx.auth.userId` — the server-derived identity
([never client-asserted](../auth/sessions-and-principals.md)).

## Seed deterministically

```json source=demos/todo/snapback/seed.json
{
  "tables": {
    "todos": [
      { "_id": "seed_todo_1", "title": "Read the Snapback explainer", "completed": true, "userId": "user_ada" },
      { "_id": "seed_todo_2", "title": "Build the todo demo", "completed": false, "userId": "user_ada" },
      { "_id": "seed_todo_3", "title": "Write the diary", "completed": false, "userId": "user_ada" },
      { "_id": "seed_todo_4", "title": "Plan the kanban demo", "completed": false, "userId": "user_grace" }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Generate and load

```sh
node packages/snapback-codegen/index.mjs myapp/snapback
```

Codegen **fails closed**: on any error it writes nothing (no silent stale
output) and exits 1 with stable diagnostic codes (`QUERY_UNKNOWN_FIELD`,
`FUNCTION_RESERVED_EXPORT`, ...). On success it writes
`myapp/snapback/generated/` — server manifests
(`schema.manifest.json`, `functions.manifest.json`), the client binding
surface (`api.mjs` + `api.d.ts`), Contract binding modules under
`contract/`, per-function argument schemas under `operations/`, and
`artifacts.json` carrying the `inputsHash` freshness key. Commit the tree.

A running server loads the app over its admin API — the kit client wraps
the endpoints:

```js source=demos/todo/surfaces/headless/run.mjs
  await db.loadSchema(gen('schema.manifest.json'));
  await db.loadFunctions(gen('functions.manifest.json'));
  await db.reset();
  await db.seed(JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(backendDir, 'seed.json'), 'utf8')));
```

(`db.ensureApp({ schema, functions, seed })` is the idempotent form —
provisions only what's missing, seeds only empty tables.)

Then call it. Function references are the generated `api.<name>` objects
from `generated/api.mjs`, and mutations return structured results:

```js source=demos/todo/tests/acceptance/headless.mjs
    const created = await db.mutate(api.createTodo, { args: { title: 'Buy milk' }, userId: ADA });
```

Continue with [the authoring loop](./the-authoring-loop.md) for the full
edit-regenerate-test cycle, and
[testing/acceptance](../testing/acceptance.md) for the harness.

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not hand-wire HTTP glue for app data.** The generated `api.mjs`
  references plus the kit client (or the Contract adapter /
  React arm) are the product path; raw `fetch` against `/query/...` is how
  demos accumulated unauditable glue before the kit existed.
- **Do not edit anything under `generated/`.** Regenerate. The server
  rejects stale artifacts loudly (`SNAPBACK_STALE_SCHEMA_ARTIFACT_VERSION`,
  `SNAPBACK_STALE_CONTRACT_DATA_INPUTS_HASH`).
- **Do not set `_createdAt`/`_updatedAt`/`_id`/`_version`.** Server-owned;
  declaring them in a schema is a hard error.
- **Do not assert identity from the client.** `ctx.auth.userId` is derived
  server-side; see [auth](../auth/sessions-and-principals.md).

# The authoring loop

> **Local target only.** This page describes the local dev/test target.
> Hosted targets make deliberately weaker or different claims — see
> [auth/targets](../auth/targets.md).

The cycle you repeat while building on Snapback:

```text
edit snapback/*.mjs  ->  regenerate  ->  run the acceptance suite  ->  inspect
```

## 1. Edit

Change `schema.mjs`, `functions.mjs`, `handlers.mjs`, or `seed.json`
([your first backend](./your-first-backend.md) covers each).

## 2. Regenerate

```sh
node packages/snapback-codegen/index.mjs <app>/snapback
```

Codegen is deterministic and **fails closed** — on error it writes nothing
and exits 1 with stable diagnostic codes on stderr, so there is never
silently stale output. On success it prints the `inputsHash` freshness key.
Commit `generated/` with your source change: the server compares hashes and
rejects stale artifacts loudly (`SNAPBACK_STALE_SCHEMA_ARTIFACT_VERSION`,
`SNAPBACK_STALE_CONTRACT_DATA_INPUTS_HASH`) rather than serving them.

If you forget this step, the very first server load or acceptance run tells
you; nothing downstream guesses.

## 3. Run the acceptance suite

Headless first — the required surface is driveable without any UI
(LLP 0012). A suite boots its own isolated server and drives the real
product path:

```sh
node <app>/tests/acceptance/headless.mjs
```

Exit `0` = every declared check passed; `1` = a check failed or the run was
short (zero checks can never pass); `2` = setup error. See
[testing/acceptance](../testing/acceptance.md) for the harness and server
lifecycle discipline.

For a demo in this repo, the whole-repo proof is
`scripts/verify-local-proof` (add `SNAPBACK_VERIFY_EXACT=0` for a
deliberately core-only iteration; merge CI requires the Exact-gated block).

## 4. Inspect

A running server tells you what it is actually serving:

```sh
cargo run                      # prints the admin URL on startup
curl http://127.0.0.1:4287/inspect
```

`GET /inspect` is the public projection (instance, capability facts);
`GET /_snapback/api/inspect` is the admin-gated full view, and the admin
console renders the same surface in a browser — the author's debugger for
"what schema/functions/data does this server hold right now". Structured
failures everywhere carry stable `SNAPBACK_*` diagnostic codes
(`{ code, severity, subsystem, message, details }`), so match on
`error.diagnostic.code`, never on message text.

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not hand-edit `generated/` or skip the regenerate step** — the
  server's stale-artifact rejection exists because "it probably still
  matches" was wrong often enough.
- **Do not assert on diagnostic message strings.** Codes are the contract;
  messages are prose.
- **Do not point a new suite at a server you didn't start.** Suites own
  their server lifecycle; see
  [testing/acceptance](../testing/acceptance.md).

# Live queries

> **Local target only.** This page describes the local dev/test target.
> Hosted targets make deliberately weaker or different claims — see
> [auth/targets](../auth/targets.md).

A live query is an ordinary query definition that clients can subscribe
to: subscribers get an authoritative initial snapshot **with** the
subscription (never a prime race), then server-pushed updates over the
durable lane as commits change the result.

## Define one

Mark the definition live — declarative or JS style
([your first backend](../getting-started/your-first-backend.md) covers the
two styles):

```js source=demos/todo/snapback/functions.mjs
export const listTodos = defineJsLiveQuery({
  args: {},
  source: 'handlers.mjs',
  exportName: 'listTodos',
  reads: ['todos'],
  authScopeField: 'userId',
```

`defineLiveQuery` is the declarative twin (same spec as `defineQuery` plus
`defaultLive: false` to make live opt-in per subscription). `reads:` and
`authScopeField:` matter: they drive invalidation and per-principal scoping
(see [auth](../auth/sessions-and-principals.md)). Subscribing to a non-live
function fails with `SNAPBACK_FUNCTION_NOT_LIVE`.

## Subscribe

`client.liveQuery(ref, options)` returns a handle with the snapshot already
applied — `rows`, `connection`, `poll()`, `dispose()`:

```js source=demos/todo/tests/acceptance/headless.mjs
    const handle = await db.liveQuery(api.listTodos, { connectionId: 'client_a', userId: ADA });
    assertEqual(handle.rows.length, 3, 'snapshot rows');
```

Cross-client delivery is the point — one client mutates, the other's
subscription updates:

```js source=demos/todo/tests/acceptance/headless.mjs
    const b = await db.liveQuery(api.listTodos, { connectionId: 'client_b', userId: ADA });
    assertEqual(b.rows.length, 3, 'b initial');
    await db.mutate(api.createTodo, { args: { title: 'Added by another client' }, userId: ADA });
    const rows = await b.poll();
    assertEqual(rows.length, 4, 'b did not receive realtime update');
```

Key options: `transport: 'stream'` for durable WebSocket push (`'poll'` is
the default, cadence `pollCadenceMs`, with `fallbackToPoll` when a stream
can't be established), `onUpdate(rows, meta)`, `onConnectionChange`,
`connectionId` (one shared socket per connection id multiplexes all of that
connection's live handles), and per-socket `stream:` tuning
(heartbeat/freshness/reconnect). Always `dispose()` handles you created.

## What arrives: replace and delta

Durable updates carry a `meta.kind`: `live_replace` (a full snapshot of the
result) or `live_delta` (incremental add/remove — the analyzable
unordered/filtered subset gets deltas; ordered queries fall back to
replace; LLP 0008 §DK-3). `resync_required` tells the client to
re-snapshot; `authorization_invalidation` is the auth barrier
([protecting data](../auth/sessions-and-principals.md)). A subscription
asserts on delta kinds like this:

```js source=demos/_kit/tests/live-delta-e2e.mjs
  const handle = await db.liveQuery('listMine', {
    connectionId: 'delta_conn',
    userId: ADA,
    transport: 'stream',
    stream: { heartbeatIntervalMs: 200, freshnessBudgetMs: 800, reconnectBaseDelayMs: 100, reconnectMaxDelayMs: 400 },
    onUpdate: rec.onUpdate,
  });
```

## Connection state an author can observe

The stream manager emits `'connecting'`, `'open'`, `'lost'`
(`{ wasOpen }`), `'budget-missed'` (socket claims open but the freshness
budget lapsed), and `'closed'`. The kit derives a per-query `connection`
axis from these and pushes it through `onConnectionChange`; the conventional
author-facing mapping (from the cursors-web hook) is:

```ts source=demos/cursors-web/surfaces/react/src/useCursorRoom.ts
export type ConnectionAxis = 'connecting' | 'live' | 'stale' | 'disconnected';
```

`open → live`; `budget-missed`/`lost → stale` (degraded — render retained
data, marked); `closed → disconnected`. Defaults:
`LIVE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000`, `LIVE_FRESHNESS_BUDGET_MS = 15_000`,
reconnect backoff 250ms → 10s. The [clients pages](../clients/contract-adapter.md)
show each arm consuming this axis.

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not poll a query you can subscribe to.** `liveQuery` exists;
  hand-rolled `setInterval` re-query loops re-derive a worse version of the
  poll transport and never get durable push.
- **Do not treat a socket as fresh because it is open.** `budget-missed`
  exists precisely because "open" and "fresh" diverge; consume the
  connection axis, not `isOpen()`.
- **Do not leak handles.** Every `liveQuery`/overlay handle is `dispose()`d
  in teardown (React: effect cleanup; suites: `cleanups`).

# Recipe: presence cursors

> **Local target only.** This page describes the local dev/test target.
> Hosted targets make deliberately weaker or different claims — see
> [auth/targets](../auth/targets.md).

"Two users see each other's cursors" is ephemeral state, not app data: it
lives in typed in-memory rooms with TTL expiry and connection-owned
cleanup (LLP 0013) — never in tables, never polled. The working reference
is `demos/cursors-web`.

## 1. Declare the ephemeral collection in the schema

An ephemeral collection is declared beside your tables, with its scope
(the room key), keying, TTL, payload budget, and publish rate all typed
and enforced server-side. The shape (this one is todo-v2's presence
collection; cursors-web's `webCursors` follows the same form):

```js source=demos/todo-v2/snapback/schema.mjs
  ephemeral: defineEphemeral({
    todoPresence: ephemeral.collection({
      scope: { listId: v.string() },
      routing: ['listId'],
      key: 'connection',
      ttlMs: 20_000,
      maxTtlMs: 30_000,
      maxValueBytes: 512,
      publishRate: { sustainedHz: 20, burst: 40 },
      delivery: { mode: 'latest', dispatchMs: 33 },
      value: v.object({
        name: v.string(),
        editing: v.optional(v.boolean()),
      }),
      publish: allow.all(),
      subscribe: allow.all(),
```

`key: 'connection'` makes the lease key the publisher's connection id —
presence provenance for free: an entry with your connection id *is* you.
Regenerate after editing (the generated publish descriptor carries the
budget facts your client code should assert against, e.g. cursors-web
checks its declared publish rate fits `sustainedHz` at init).

## 2. Subscribe to the room

`subscribeEphemeral` returns an overlay that applies the authoritative
snapshot, then buffers and applies deltas from the shared live socket
(registered before the snapshot request, so nothing can fall in the gap):

```ts source=demos/cursors-web/surfaces/react/src/useCursorRoom.ts
    void client
      .subscribeEphemeral(cursorsRef, { connectionId, scope: { roomId } })
      .then((overlay) => {
        if (disposed) {
          // StrictMode double-mount: the first effect's subscribe may resolve
          // after its cleanup ran — never leak that overlay's lane consumer.
          overlay.dispose();
          return;
        }
        overlayRef.current = overlay;
        subscribedRef.current = true;
        offChange = overlay.onChange(handleChange);
        recompute();
      })
```

Read entries with `overlay.currentEntries()` — each is
`{ key, value, expiresAtMs, ... }`; `entry.key === connectionId` is
"self". `onChange` also delivers a level-triggered `'needs_resync'` when
connection continuity is lost (epoch boundary / queue overflow): present
degraded state, then re-enter with a fresh `subscribeEphemeral` and swap
the overlay.

## 3. Publish samples under the declared budget

```ts source=demos/cursors-web/surfaces/react/src/useCursorRoom.ts
      overlay
        .publish(value, { ttlMs: PRESENCE_TTL_MS })
        .then(() => {
          state.published += 1;
          if (state.establishedAtMs === null) state.establishedAtMs = Date.now();
        })
        .catch(() => {
          state.rejected += 1;
        });
```

The server enforces the schema's rate and payload budgets — count
rejections rather than retrying blindly. Entries expire on the
server-stamped `expiresAtMs`; the reference hook freezes TTL-pruning while
the connection is `stale`/`disconnected` so departed cursors stay
renderable during degradation instead of silently vanishing.

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not store presence in tables.** Cursor positions in app data means
  commits, versions, and history for state that is worthless in ten
  seconds; the ephemeral store exists for exactly this.
- **Do not invent your own presence keys.** `key: 'connection'` gives you
  provenance; a custom name field is spoofable and duplicates on refresh.
- **Do not publish above the declared budget** — assert your sample rate
  fits the generated budget facts at init, like the reference hook does.

# Recipe: hidden hands

> **Local target only.** This page describes the local dev/test target.
> Hosted targets make deliberately weaker or different claims — see
> [auth/targets](../auth/targets.md).

Per-principal secrecy over shared data: a card game where every player
queries the same `myHand` function and sees only their own cards — live,
across logout, and honestly offline. The working reference is
`demos/card-game`, and every claim here is asserted by its acceptance
suite (which runs in the local proof).

Prerequisite: sessions-mode auth —
[sessions and principals](../auth/sessions-and-principals.md).

## One query, disjoint worlds

Each player signs in (email code → session) and calls the same query with
no owner argument; the server stamps the session principal and the
`authScopeField` does the rest:

```js source=demos/card-game/tests/acceptance/authority-scope.mjs
  const [adaResult, graceResult] = await Promise.all([
    ada.client.query('myHand', { args: { gameId } }),
    grace.client.query('myHand', { args: { gameId } }),
  ]);
```

The suite then asserts the two result sets are disjoint — no card leaks
across principals, finite or live.

## Logout blanks yours, only yours

```js source=demos/card-game/tests/acceptance/authority-scope.mjs
  await ada.client.authLogout();
  assert.deepEqual(adaSurface.boundary.current('hand'), []);
  assert.deepEqual(
    graceSurface.boundary.current('hand').map(({ card }) => card),
    ['king-clubs', 'ten-diamonds'],
  );
```

The invalidation barrier is per-principal and immediate on live
boundaries (LLP 0053).

## Offline retention ends at the lease deadline, exactly

With a client store, an authorized retained query survives a cold process
start while the server is down — readable, marked `stale` — until the
signed lease's client deadline, after which store validation deletes the
hidden rows before any fallback could serve them:

```js source=demos/card-game/tests/acceptance/authority-scope.mjs
  const offlineSurface = await trackSurface(coldGraceOptions);
  assert.equal(offlineSurface.retained(), true);
  assert.equal(offlineSurface.connection(), 'stale');
```

```js source=demos/card-game/tests/acceptance/authority-scope.mjs
  const expiredState = await coldGraceStore.snapshot();
  assert.equal(expiredState.retained[retainedQueryKey], undefined);
  assert.equal(expiredState.queryAuthorization[retainedQueryKey]?.lease, null);
```

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not filter secrets client-side.** Sending the whole game state and
  hiding other hands in the UI is not secrecy; the scoping must be the
  server's.
- **Do not cache authorized rows outside the client store.** The store is
  what enforces the lease deadline; a side cache outlives authorization.
- **Do not pass the player as a query argument.** The server derives the
  principal; an owner argument is spoofable and is rejected in sessions
  mode.

# Acceptance testing

> **Local target only.** This page describes the local dev/test target.
> Hosted targets make deliberately weaker or different claims — see
> [auth/targets](../auth/targets.md).

Snapback apps are proven **headless-first** (LLP 0012): the required
surface is a suite that boots a real server, loads the real generated
artifacts, and drives the product client — no UI in the loop. UI arms
(Contract, React) are additional surfaces over the same backend.

## The harness

`demos/_kit/harness.mjs` provides a dependency-free suite with structured,
machine-readable results and **vacuous-pass protection** — a run that
executes zero checks (or fewer than it declared) can never report success:

```js source=demos/_kit/harness.mjs
    finish() {
      const passed = results.filter((r) => r.ok).length;
      const total = results.length;
      // ENG-22486: zero checks (or a short run against a declared count) can
      // never be a pass — a pre-check throw that skips the checks must fail.
      let shortfall = null;
      if (total === 0) {
        shortfall = 'zero checks ran';
      } else if (expectedChecks !== null && total !== expectedChecks) {
        shortfall = `ran ${total}/${expectedChecks} expected checks`;
      }
      const ok = passed === total && shortfall === null;
```

Use `createSuite(title, { expectedChecks })` and `await suite.check(name,
fn)` per behavior; `runAcceptance(suite, body, { cleanups })` is the shared
runner tail — it surfaces setup errors with their stacks, prints a
machine-readable JSON report line, runs cleanups in reverse order, and
exits `0` (pass), `1` (check failure or short run), or `2` (setup error).
Assertion helpers: `assert`, `assertEqual`, and
`assertThrows(fn, code, msg)`, which matches `error.diagnostic.code` —
stable codes, never message text. `requireBunRuntime(label)` guards suites
that must run under bun.

## Server lifecycle: isolated, provenance-verified, owned

`startServer` from `demos/_kit/server-process.mjs` is the only way a suite
should obtain a server:

```js source=demos/todo/tests/acceptance/headless.mjs
const server = await startServer({ port: 4399, db: ':memory:', cwd: repoRoot,
  provenance: { appId: 'todo', artifactsPath: join(repoRoot, 'demos', 'todo', 'snapback', 'generated', 'artifacts.json') } });
const db = new SnapbackClient(server.baseUrl, server.clientOptions);
```

What it guarantees:

- **Isolated ports by default.** Ordinary starts pass `--port 0`, so the OS
  assigns a port and the child reports its actual bound URL through a ready
  file; always use the returned `server.baseUrl`, never the port you asked
  for.
- **Reuse only with verified provenance.** A server already listening is
  reused only when its loaded bundle identity matches the declared
  `provenance` (or `binaryProvenance`); any mismatch — or no declared
  identity — refuses reuse and spawns a fresh isolated server instead.
- **Owned teardown.** The returned handle's `.stop()` tears down the whole
  process tree the harness itself started (SIGTERM then SIGKILL, attested
  group exit). Nothing else is ever killed.
- `--memory` for `db: ':memory:'`; file-backed servers take an exclusive
  sidecar lock so two servers can't mutate one database.

Then load and drive the app exactly as production clients do — see
[your first backend](../getting-started/your-first-backend.md) for
`loadSchema`/`loadFunctions`/`reset`/`seed` and the query/mutation calls,
and [realtime/live-queries](../realtime/live-queries.md) for asserting on
live updates.

## What a good suite asserts

The todo headless suite (`demos/todo/tests/acceptance/headless.mjs`) is the
model: authoritative reads after writes, structured mutation results
(`result`, `changed_count`), server-owned system fields, live snapshot +
cross-client realtime delivery, error paths by diagnostic code, and
admin-gated operations with the server-issued `server.adminToken`.

## Anti-patterns

- **Do not claim a fixed port and kill whatever holds it.** Request an
  OS-assigned port (the default); reuse a server only after provenance
  verification; stop only processes your own harness started.
  `server-process.mjs` implements exactly this discipline — inherit it.
- **Do not swallow setup errors into a green run.** Zero-check and
  short-run passes are structurally impossible under the harness; keep
  `expectedChecks` declared so they stay impossible.
- **Do not assert on diagnostic message text.** Use `assertThrows(fn,
  'SNAPBACK_...')` against the code.
